strengths: Novel algorithmic approach: Departs from standard dynamic programming for treewidth algorithms, instead combining structural characterization of SCMs with linear programming. This is genuinely innovative and could inspire applications beyond this domain.

Comprehensive complexity characterization: Provides a complete and systematic map of tractability across the 3×3 expressivity matrix, precisely delineating which fragments are tractable under which parameterizations.

Tight theoretical bounds: Each positive result is paired with matching hardness results, demonstrating that identified tractability boundaries are sharp and cannot be improved under standard complexity assumptions.

Technically sound contributions: The LP-based formulations (Theorems 5, 11) are well-crafted, the structural characterization in Lemma 10 is non-trivial, and hardness reductions are correct and appropriate.
Clear presentation and relevance: Well-written paper with effective visualizations (Figure 1), addressing an important framework (PCH) central to modern causal reasoning in AI.
Opens new research directions: Identifies first gateways to tractability for a problem that was computationally intractable in almost all classical settings.
weaknesses: Severely limited practical applicability: No experimental validation on any instances. The algorithms have prohibitive complexity in practice (LP with O(n·d^w) variables for Theorem 5; trying n! orderings with d^(n²)-sized LPs for Theorem 11), making them impractical except for tiny instances. Model construction also involves exponentially large hidden variable domains.

Restricted to linear fragments only: Results apply exclusively to L^lin_prob and L^lin_counterfact. Polynomial constraints (L^poly) remain ∃R-hard even with proposed parameters, excluding a significant and important class of formulas. No discussion of approximation or heuristics for intractable cases.

Cannot extend to marginalization operators: Results do not extend to full summation operators (crucial for expressing many real causal queries) without bounding nesting depth—a significant limitation acknowledged but not resolved.

Insufficient analysis of fundamental barriers: Theorem 9 shows NP-hardness for L^lin_causal on vertex-disjoint paths; this suggests deeper intractability. No exploration of alternative parameters (pathwidth, vertex cover, etc.) or whether these might improve tractability.

Gap between theory and practice: Entirely theoretical with no bridge to implementation. No guidance for practitioners, no solvers proposed, no identification of when these results might be useful in practice.

Incomplete technical exposition: Lemma 10's structural characterization lacks intuitive motivation for why hidden variables must capture all functions. Observation 4's reduction of domain size makes implicit assumptions about function representation that should be stated explicitly.

strengths: First systematic parameterized complexity analysis of causal satisfiability, identifying genuine tractability islands for a known-hard problem
Novel algorithmic approach departing from standard dynamic programming: uses structural characterization combined with linear programming, which could find broader applications
Comprehensive and tight complexity landscape: matching upper and lower bounds across key fragments with rigorous proofs and appropriate hardness reductions
Strong technical contributions including non-trivial structural lemmas (Lemma 10) establishing the existence of well-structured SCMs for counterfactual instances
Clear presentation with effective visualizations (Figure 1) and informative examples (Example 6) that illustrate the constructions
Transparent discussion of limitations and honest treatment of gaps (e.g., restriction to linear inequalities, bounded marginalization nesting depth)
weaknesses: Limited practical applicability: no empirical validation or demonstration of real-world use cases where parameters (treewidth, number of variables) would be small enough for tractability to matter
Restriction to linear inequalities: main tractability results only cover L^lin fragments; polynomial inequalities (L^poly) remain ∃R-hard even with parameters, leaving a significant expressivity gap

Severe algorithmic inefficiency in Theorem 11: requires trying all n! variable orderings, yielding runtime n! · d^O(n²) · |ϕ|^O(1), which is prohibitively expensive in practice and inadequately discussed
Incremental contribution within scope: applies standard parameterized complexity frameworks to a known-hard problem; the LP-based technique, while novel, is somewhat domain-specific
Incomplete coverage: no FPT results for SAT^base_prob (only XP or hardness), cannot extend to SATlin_causal with treewidth alone, and marginalization handling limited to bounded nesting depth

Missing practical validation: no experiments on benchmark instances, no comparison with other approaches, and unclear whether LP constructions are implementable efficiently for realistic problem sizes
Technical scaling concerns: LP formulations have O(n·d^w) variables and constraints, which could be prohibitively large even for moderate width w and domain size d

strengths: Novel application of parameterized complexity to causal reasoning satisfiability, addressing an important computational challenge in causal inference
Complete characterization of tractability landscape across PCH expressivity matrix with tight upper and lower bounds demonstrating results are fundamental
Innovative algorithmic techniques departing from standard dynamic programming paradigm, using linear programming to combine discrete and continuous structures—potentially valuable for other problems
Rigorous technical treatment with non-trivial structural characterizations (e.g., Lemma 10 on well-structured models) and careful complexity analyses
Clear presentation with effective motivation and helpful visual summary (Figure 1) of the complexity landscape
weaknesses: Complete absence of experimental validation: no implementation, benchmarks, or empirical evaluation of algorithm performance, limiting credibility of practical utility

Severe practical limitations inadequately discussed: Theorem 11's n! factor is prohibitively expensive even for moderate n; algorithms for Theorem 5 have running times d^f(tw)|φ|^O(1) with no evidence domain size d is small in practice
No evidence or discussion that primal treewidth is realistically bounded in causal models of interest, raising questions about when tractability results apply

Limited scope: results only cover base and lin fragments, not the more expressive poly fragment; for counterfactuals only linear fragments are handled; marginalization with bounded nesting depth mentioned but underdeveloped
Implicit doubly-exponential domain size for the hidden variable U in Lemma 10 (d^d^(n-1)) deserves explicit discussion and is inadequately emphasized; significantly impacts practical applicability

Hardness results use relatively standard reduction techniques (k-Multicolored-Clique, 3-SAT, ETR) with limited conceptual novelty; Theorem 2 shows hardness only on highly restricted instances (single variable or edgeless graph)
Missing practical considerations: no discussion of LP solver numerical stability, construction efficiency, or performance on the specific sparse LP instances arising from the algorithm
No comparison with baseline approaches, heuristics, or existing tools; unclear how algorithms perform relative to brute-force or general-purpose solvers
